result.title: PGGT-Loc: Primitive-Grounded Geometry Transformer for Feed-Forward Camera Localization
result.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 24 pages, 14 figures, including appendices. Code and models: https://github.com/3dv-casia/PGGT-Loc
result.summary: Camera localization methods are mostly multi-stage pipelines relying on dedicated and complex maps that are costly to construct, store, and maintain over time. Alternatively, well-structured maps that organize scenes with compact yet expressive primitives are often readily available, providing rich structural and semantic cues that humans can interpret. However, their potential for direct camera localization remains largely unexplored due to the significant modality gap between map primitives and visual observations. This motivates a new concept for localization, which estimates camera poses by grounding query observations to map primitives. In this paper, we instantiate the concept in the context of planar primitives with PGGT, the Primitive-Grounded Geometry Transformer network. Given a single query image and a set of planar map primitives, the network is trained to predict multiple localization targets for feed-forward 6-DoF camera localization that generalizes to unseen environments. With this straightforward and scalable architecture, our method pushes the state-of-the-art localization performance on both dense surface maps and minimal layout models. The code and models are available at https://github.com/3dv-casia/PGGT-Loc

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PGGT，用单张查询图像与平面地图基元直接回归 6-DoF 相机位姿，避免依赖复杂多阶段地图，在密集表面地图与极简 layout 模型上取得领先定位性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「视觉观测对齐到紧凑几何基元」的思路，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据与结构化任务要素如何绑定进内部表征提供参照；但该文属前馈位姿回归、无 latent 推理过程，内部表征是否编码对应关系仍需核查。
